page: Microsoft Azure B16ps_v2 is a burstable general purpose virtual machine running on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz, the instance provides 16 physical cores across 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, resulting in a balanced allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators, depending entirely on remote storage volumes for system and data persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, the B16ps_v2 demonstrates mid-tier multi-core computing capability, reaching a multi-core Geekbench score of 9576.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 28877.71. Single-threaded throughput is comparatively modest, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 1107.0 and a single-core stress-ng score of 1822.49. Cryptographic tasks run efficiently with native hardware AES support, though PassMark CPU encryption scores register in the lower quartile at 2608.59.

Memory and network-adjacent operations show consistent middle-range performance, with uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 130.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieving 67.46 GB/sec. Application testing records static web serving throughput of 18.84 GB/sec and Redis SET operations of 21.22 million operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference is limited by the lack of specialized vector instructions such as AVX-512 or AMX, producing low-tier prompt processing speeds across small and medium language models.

Because it couples a burstable CPU credit scheme with 16 dedicated physical cores and 64 GB of memory, the B16ps_v2 offers high resource density without requiring constant peak CPU billing. The instance is suited for variable or intermittent workloads such as code compilation pipelines, intermediate database services, static web serving clusters, and dev/test environments.
